definitions.gloss: rakugo storyteller; rakugo performer; professional raconteur
definitions.explanation: A professional performer of rakugo, a traditional Japanese art of comic storytelling where a single seated performer plays all characters using only a fan and a small cloth as props.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}な{噺家|はなしか}の{公演|こうえん}を{見|み}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to see a performance by a famous rakugo storyteller.

examples.japanese: {噺家|はなしか}になるには、{師匠|ししょう}に{弟子入|でしい}りしなければならない。
examples.english: To become a rakugo performer, you must become an apprentice to a master.

examples.japanese: その{噺家|はなしか}は{一人|ひとり}で{何役|なんやく}も{演|えん}じ{分|わ}けて、{客席|きゃくせき}を{大|おお}いに{沸|わ}かせた。
examples.english: The storyteller played multiple characters by himself and had the audience in stitches.

notes:
The character {噺|はなし} is a Japanese-coined kanji ({国字|こくじ}) meaning "story" or "tale," composed of {口|くち} (mouth) + {新|しん} (new). Combined with {家|か} (professional, expert), it literally means "story professional."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {噺家|はなしか}になる: to become a rakugo performer
- {噺家|はなしか}の{高座|こうざ}: a storyteller's stage performance
- {若手|わかて}{噺家|はなしか}: young/up-and-coming rakugo performer
- {真打|しんうち}の{噺家|はなしか}: a master-level rakugo performer

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Rakugo performers follow a strict apprenticeship system with ranks: {前座|ぜんざ} (opener), {二|に}ツ{目|め} (mid-rank), and {真打|しんうち} (master). The tradition has roots going back to the Edo period and continues to thrive today.

SIMILAR TERMS:
- {落語家|らくごか}: rakugo performer — synonym using the more common word for the art form
- {話家|はなしか}: storyteller — alternate kanji spelling, less common
